source.title: Curvature-guided anisotropic noise injection for robust multimodal data processing in neuroscience and perception science

record.tranche_reason: Tests large-batch generalization and optimizer comparisons in multimodal benchmark settings, extending the claim to multimodal datasets and stress tests.
record.gate_note: Table 2 reports test accuracy for four datasets across optimizers and batch sizes. Other cited studies and theoretical claims are not this study's results. Rows cover benchmark test accuracy only; stress-test values are described without exact numbers in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own batch-size and optimizer comparisons on image-based multimodal classification tasks, bearing on V4 and V5. Tuning protocols and equal epoch budgets are unspecified, limiting what these comparisons establish.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors attribute large-batch generalization and robustness deficits to insufficient geometric exploration, and conclude that GANI improves accuracy and sensory-corruption robustness while approaching SAM's performance with about 2.5% throughput overhead. Their claimed mechanisms are stronger than what the reported comparisons alone establish. GANI reduces, rather than fully eliminates, the clean-accuracy deficit relative to small-batch SGD on all four benchmarks.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes GANI, an EMA-based curvature estimate and anisotropic noise injection method, and evaluates it against large-batch and small-batch optimizers in multimodal settings; the cited original studies are not reproduced.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports different test accuracy across datasets and optimizer choices; batch size is 128 for Small-batch SGD and 4,096 for the other Table 2 methods.

fits_no_version.finding: LARS, SAM, and GANI recover varying amounts of accuracy relative to large-batch SGD in Table 2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alternative large-batch optimization methods can improve held-out accuracy under the reported training setup; these comparisons alone do not establish equal-budget recovery.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 associates lower estimated RLCT with lower test error; Sections 5.5.1–5.5.2 report Hessian eigenvalues and filter-normalized loss landscapes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selected optimizer outcomes associate flatter geometry or lower estimated RLCT with better test performance. This does not establish V7's specific sharpness measure or comparative ranking of generalization gaps.

fits_no_version.finding: GANI performs better under visual corruption and missing textual embeddings in the declared omitted stress tests.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects robustness to corrupted or missing modalities.

record.problems: The study's optimizer comparisons do not report tuning protocols, training accuracy, or epoch budgets. The large-versus-small batch comparison changes batch size but gives no fixed-epoch condition. Detailed stress-test outcomes are described without exact numeric values in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No Table 2 result rows were omitted. Figure-only stress-test values were not extracted as exact values; the text gives only selected qualitative descriptions and one bound for the large-batch SGD visual-noise result.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps and behavior beyond the width required for interpolation.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected comparisons, local connectivity, and initialization effects.

The limited-tuning condition is unverified. No training-performance comparison for Adam or RMSprop, momentum-SGD comparison, broader tuning intervention, decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching, or word-level language modeling.
Equal epoch budgets are unverified; no batch-size threshold sweep or controlled tests of longer training, learning-rate scaling, normalization changes, or the named recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on data size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking of generalization gaps at similarly low training loss, including comparison against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of highly memorized examples compared with equally sized random removals.

missing.what: Table 1's MNIST Tanh-MLP batch comparison: batch 64 SGD has train loss 0.045 ± 0.004 and test error 1.82 ± 0.08%; batch 1,024 SGD has train loss 0.012 ± 0.002 and test error 3.15 ± 0.14%. These are additional batch-size results, not declared omitted.

record.verdict_notes: All Table 2 numerical values match the supplied text. Optimizers are training procedures, not model subjects; FCNN, MobileNet, GoogLeNet, and ResNet-50 denote visual backbones within fusion systems. The flagship textual input is generated from class labels using frozen BERT, which materially limits interpretation as ordinary held-out image classification. No fixed-epoch or limited-tuning protocol can be inferred from convergence plots, cosine-annealing descriptions, or algorithmic warmup alone. Missing protocol information belongs under untested, not as a separate limits_scope verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.

Image-classification and language settings beyond the four multimodal benchmarks; momentum SGD; limited-tuning protocol; training performance; broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching optimizers, and word-level language models.
Fixed epoch budgets are not specified. Longer training, learning-rate scaling with warmup, normalization or regularization changes, and same-epoch recipe adaptations are not tested.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of memorized examples and resulting test accuracy.

relationships.condition: Adam on all four multimodal benchmarks and RMSprop on MNIST-Sem., SVHN-context, and CIFAR-10-VT, all at batch size 4,096
relationships.reason: R3–R4, R10–R11, R17–R18, and R25 report higher accuracy than same-batch SGD; these qualify the worse-generalization tendency, but unspecified tuning prevents a direct challenge to its limited-tuning condition.
relationships.display_finding: Reported advantages for Adam across all four benchmarks and RMSprop across three remain unverified, with tuning unspecified.

relationships.condition: RMSprop versus SGD on CIFAR-100-VT at batch size 4,096, under the reported but unspecified tuning protocol
relationships.reason: R24 reports 71.50% accuracy versus R23's 72.18%, agreeing with the predicted direction; significance and the limited-tuning condition are unverified.
relationships.display_finding: Reported accuracy favored SGD over RMSprop, but the comparison remains unverified and neither significance nor the tuning scope was established.

relationships.condition: Reported SGD comparisons between batches 128 and 4,096 on four multimodal benchmarks; epoch budgets unspecified
relationships.reason: R1–R2, R8–R9, R15–R16, and R22–R23 show accuracy penalties of 0.67, 2.53, 3.85, and 5.23 percentage points; this supports the batch-penalty direction without establishing the fixed-epoch condition.
relationships.display_finding: The study's comparisons suggest lower accuracy with larger batches across the multimodal benchmarks, without establishing equal epoch budgets. These comparisons have not been verified.

relationships.condition: Single-hidden-layer Tanh MLP on MNIST, batches 64 versus 1,024, trained to their respective converged minima
relationships.reason: Text and Table 1, missing from the rows, report test error rising from 1.82% to 3.15% despite training loss falling from 0.045 to 0.012; equal epoch budgets are not established.
relationships.display_finding: The study's comparison suggests higher test error despite lower training loss at the larger batch, without establishing equal epoch budgets. This comparison has not been verified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Adam and RMSprop versus same-batch Large-batch SGD across the four Table 2 benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: Adam's test accuracy exceeds Large-batch SGD on all four datasets (R4, R11, R18, R25); RMSprop exceeds it on three and is lower on CIFAR-100-VT (R3, R10, R17, R24). This contradicts the worse-held-out-performance direction in these settings.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Batch size 4,096 versus 128 for Large-batch SGD and Small-batch SGD across the four Table 2 benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: Large-batch SGD has lower test accuracy than Small-batch SGD on all four datasets (R1-R2, R8-R9, R15-R16, R22-R23). The paper does not state an epoch budget.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The study does not report a fixed-epoch comparison or test the recipe adaptations named in V5, so its results do not establish the version's fixed-epoch condition (R1-R2, R8-R9, R15-R16, R22-R23).
